content:
Aiyana Brooks-Tan
Frontend Developer | React & TypeScript
Dublin, Ireland | aiyana.brookstan@example.com | +353 55 555 0404
GitHub: github.com/aiyana-bt-example | Portfolio: aiyana-bt.example.com

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Early-career web developer with hands-on experience building React interfaces and accessible web features. Experience includes improving accessibility across 20+ components, creating a reusable component with Storybook stories, and writing unit tests with Jest and React Testing Library. Project work includes TypeScript, Node.js, Next.js and PostgreSQL listed among technical skills. Interested in building straightforward, accessible experiences for users.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages and web: JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3
Frontend: React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS
Backend and databases: Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL
Testing and tools: Jest, React Testing Library, Storybook, Git, GitHub, Figma
Accessibility: WCAG 2.1

EXPERIENCE
Frontend Developer (Part-time, Freelance) | Self-employed
Oct 2025–Present
- Built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS; hosted on Vercel.
- Made small updates to two WordPress sites.

Software Development Intern | Harbourline Media, Dublin
May 2024–Aug 2024
- Worked with the web team on the company’s React news site.
- Fixed accessibility issues identified in an audit, including keyboard navigation, colour contrast and ARIA labels, across 20+ components.
- Built a reusable image gallery component and created Storybook stories for it.
- Wrote unit tests using Jest and React Testing Library.

Barista (Part-time during studies) | Corner Bean Cafe, Dublin
2021–2025

EDUCATION
BSc (Hons) Computing – Software Development | Liffey Institute of Technology
2021–2025 | First Class Honours
- Final-year project: “Tidewatch,” an accessible tide and weather app for sea swimmers, built with React, TypeScript and Node.js.
- Relevant modules: Web Development, Databases, Human-Computer Interaction, Software Testing, Data Structures & Algorithms.

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Mandarin (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, professional, well-structured early-career CV. It presents relevant React, TypeScript, accessibility, testing, Storybook, Next.js and Node.js experience in a concise format, and the First Class Honours degree strengthens the profile. The strongest evidence is specific: accessibility improvements across 20+ components, a reusable image gallery, Storybook stories, and Jest/React Testing Library tests. The main content weakness is that the summary contains awkward wording—“Project work includes TypeScript, Node.js, Next.js and PostgreSQL listed among technical skills”—rather than communicating demonstrated experience. The CV also does not clearly distinguish hands-on project experience from skills-list knowledge, which matters for this full-stack role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly standard headings, reverse-chronological experience, plain text dates, and searchable technology names. It should parse reliably and has a strong keyword base for React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Next.js, Jest, Storybook, Git, accessibility and WCAG. AI screening probability is moderate to high for a junior or early-career frontend role, but lower for this specific full-stack vacancy because the CV does not show two years of professional React/TypeScript experience, backend service implementation, end-to-end testing, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, web security, or privacy/GDPR knowledge. The document also does not explicitly use the terms “Git-based workflows,” “unit and end-to-end testing,” or “responsive layouts,” although some related evidence is present. No major formatting or parsing defect is apparent.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role’s accessibility and patient-experience themes. The audit work involving keyboard navigation, colour contrast, ARIA labels and 20+ components is particularly relevant to Verdane Care’s WCAG-focused product environment. The yoga-studio booking website provides relevant wellness and booking-domain context, and Next.js, Storybook and testing match several nice-to-have requirements. English is shown as native. However, the candidate material does not demonstrate the required 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience, backend Node.js services, SQL application work, end-to-end testing, web security fundamentals, or health-data privacy experience. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be solved by rewriting. German/Croatian, AWS/Docker and analytics/A/B testing are also not supported by the candidate information.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUE / TRUTHFULNESS AND CLARITY: In the Professional Summary, replace the sentence “Project work includes TypeScript, Node.js, Next.js and PostgreSQL listed among technical skills.” It is awkward and could imply project experience that is not clearly evidenced. Use only the supported evidence, for example: “Hands-on experience building React interfaces, improving accessibility across 20+ components, creating a reusable component with Storybook stories, and writing unit tests with Jest and React Testing Library. Academic project experience includes React, TypeScript and Node.js; additional technical skills include Next.js, Express and PostgreSQL.”

HIGH-VALUE ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENT: In the Experience section under “Frontend Developer (Part-time, Freelance),” change the booking-site bullet to explicitly connect the supported technology and domain evidence: “Built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS; hosted the site on Vercel.” This is already substantially present, but keeping “booking website,” “Next.js,” “Tailwind CSS” and “Vercel” together improves keyword matching for the role’s booking and server-side-rendering context. Do not add React, PostgreSQL, APIs or payment integrations to this bullet because they are not stated in the original candidate information.

MINOR ATS IMPROVEMENT: In the Technical Skills section, change “Languages and web” to “Languages and Web Technologies” and change “Testing and tools” to “Testing and Development Tools.” Keep the existing technologies, and write “Git and GitHub” rather than “Git, GitHub” if space permits so the Git-based workflow keyword is easier to interpret.

MINOR CONTENT IMPROVEMENT: In the Professional Summary, replace “Interested in building straightforward, accessible experiences for users” with a stronger evidence-based statement such as “Focuses on building straightforward, accessible web experiences.” This better reflects the documented accessibility work without claiming healthcare or privacy experience.
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- “Project work includes TypeScript, Node.js, Next.js and PostgreSQL” — the candidate’s material supports TypeScript and Node.js in the Tidewatch project and Next.js in the yoga-studio project, but does not support PostgreSQL being used in a project.
unsupported_claims: “Project work includes TypeScript, Node.js, Next.js and PostgreSQL” — the candidate’s material supports TypeScript and Node.js in the Tidewatch project and Next.js in the yoga-studio project, but does not support PostgreSQL being used in a project.

requirements.requirement: 2+ years of professional experience building web applications with React and TypeScript
Experience writing backend services in Node.js (Express, NestJS or similar) and working with SQL databases
Understanding of semantic HTML, responsive layouts and web accessibility basics
Experience with automated testing (unit and end-to-end) and Git-based workflows
Awareness of web security fundamentals (authentication, OWASP Top 10) and willingness to learn the privacy requirements of health data
Fluent English
German or Croatian is helpful for customer-facing conversations
Experience with Next.js or other server-side rendering frameworks

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, and professionally presented. It clearly communicates React, TypeScript, accessibility, testing, Storybook, Next.js, and the candidate’s First Class Honours degree. The internship bullets are specific and credible, particularly the accessibility work across 20+ components. The main content weakness is the duplicated sentence in the Professional Summary, which makes the opening feel careless and reduces impact. The document also presents a primarily frontend profile while the target role is full-stack; this is partly a candidate-experience gap rather than a writing defect.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, plain text formatting, clear dates, and ATS-friendly keyword placement. Relevant terms such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Jest, React Testing Library, Storybook, Git/GitHub, Next.js, WCAG 2.1, accessibility, and Vercel are present. AI/ATS screening probability is moderate to good for junior frontend or React roles, but lower for this full-stack role because the CV does not demonstrate 2+ years of React/TypeScript professional experience, end-to-end testing, web security, or privacy work. The duplicated summary paragraph may also reduce perceived quality during AI screening, although it should still parse correctly.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with React, TypeScript, accessibility, Next.js, wellness-related booking software, Storybook, unit testing, Git/GitHub, and fluent English. The yoga-studio booking website provides relevant wellness and appointment-booking context, while the Tidewatch project supports the company’s interest in accessible, straightforward user experiences. The candidate's material does not establish the required 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience. It also does not establish professional Node.js backend-service or SQL development, end-to-end testing, web security fundamentals, health-data privacy, AWS, Docker, or analytics/A-B testing. These are experience gaps, not defects that can be solved through wording. German or Croatian is not listed, so that nice-to-have is not demonstrated.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUE — In the Professional Summary section, remove the repeated sentence beginning “Hands-on experience building React interfaces...” because the same content appears twice. Replace the entire summary with one concise version, for example: “Early-career web developer with hands-on experience building React interfaces, accessible web features, and reusable components. Improved accessibility across 20+ components, created a reusable image gallery with Storybook stories, and wrote unit tests with Jest and React Testing Library. Academic project experience includes React, TypeScript, and Node.js, with additional skills in Next.js, Express, and PostgreSQL.”

MINOR ATS ENHANCEMENT — In the Technical Skills section, retain the existing keyword coverage but use consistent capitalization in the category labels: change “Backend and databases” to “Backend and Databases” and “Testing and Development Tools” to “Testing and Development Tools.” This is a small professionalism improvement and does not add unsupported skills.

MINOR ALIGNMENT ENHANCEMENT — In the Experience section under “Frontend Developer (Part-time, Freelance),” retain the existing booking-website bullet but make the wellness context explicit without overstating the work: change “Built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS; hosted the site on Vercel” to “Built and deployed a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS; hosted it on Vercel.”
critique.critical_issues: The Professional Summary contains a duplicated block of content: the claims beginning “Hands-on experience building React interfaces...” appear twice. This is a clear quality and professionalism defect and should be removed. No unsupported skills, tools, certifications, or experiences were detected when compared with the Original Candidate Information.
